content.thinking:
I'm tracing who actually owns the cursor-vs-clock validation: ADR-0012 assumes ADR-0016 handles it, but ADR-0016 doesn't, so the real owner should be ADR-0011's restore validation logic, assuming the kernel clock is set before restore runs. This looks like an unowned cross-ADR gap that needs to be flagged.

I also want to verify whether anything reads the derived state in that narrow window right after the power hook but before atmo processing, since Attention might fire there and conflict with the exactness claim elsewhere.

The real divergence I'm tracking: Attention reads P right after the power hook but before restore recomputes it, so an uninterrupted vs. interrupted tick could see different P values. The main suspect caller is Sanity's perception filter, since it's the sole non-diagnostic consumer of true_value and likely runs sim-side, which makes this divergence plausible rather than hypothetical. I should also check whether P feeds into anything persisted via the hash mechanism.

Given P depends on temperature (nRT/V), any CHILL/BURN trace that mutates persisted t also implicitly changes P — so the fix needs to recompute intensive caches (P, p_o2, o2_pm) for compartments touched by draws and by temperature-changing traces in phase 0, not just draws alone.

I'll flag this as medium severity but blocking, since the restore-equivalence table is the ADR's core contract and baking in a divergence here would be costly to unwind later — though the amendment itself is simple.

I also need to check if p_prev/trend (trend = P - p_prev) in phase 7 has the same staleness problem, since trend is supposed to be a pure function of n, V, and persisted p_prev.

Separately, I'm catching a blocking, high-severity gap: M19 and M14 are missing INIT scope entirely — WM-7 calls M19 in INIT and ADR-0017 calls M14 in INIT, but ADR-0012 only scopes M19 to APPLY and never defines INIT deposit draining. The fix is to scope M19 to APPLY and INIT, M14 to APPLY, HOOK, and INIT, with INIT deposits draining at the first power-hook tick after the LOADING→RUNNING transition.

I'm also flagging that ADR-0012's own assumption about ADR-0026 conflicts with WM-7 and ADR-0011 on whether M19 runs in a P2 apply, and that the cursor verifier is unowned since ADR-0016 has no such row — I'm assigning ownership to ADR-0011 under its restore validation steps, with an amendment adding a cursor-consistency check against restored T per ADR-0012, and retargeting ADR-0012's assumption accordingly.

There's also a tuning-offset issue: the verifier could reject saves if offsets change mid-save, so I need a stance like catalogue_version gating or tolerance for that case.

On the RNG id field sizing versus ID_MAX, I'm weighing whether to widen the field to 24 bits or just rely on a boot-time assertion since MVP has no compaction, though VS-A's compaction could push ids past current limits.

The pending_draw sort key uses an 8-bit arrival index, but the queue bound (MAX_CREW × compartments) can overflow 255 at VS-A scale even though MVP stays within range — I'd amend this with a boot assertion or widen the arrival field to 16 bits.

There's also a minor inconsistency in the TR count statement where the row totals don't add up correctly due to an extra entry, which is trivial to fix.

On the budget side, weld set overhead runs ~0.6ms per hook against a 0.5ms share target, suggesting a projected miss — the stagger assumption of equal phase splits doesn't hold since the failure hook (phases 8-11 visiting every node/edge plus descriptor build) likely exceeds a third of the budget, so S1 needs to report per-hook costs rather than per-step thirds, with acceptance gated on that reporting.

On gating scope, S1 gates the budget numbers in §13 but not the ADR's underlying design choices like the stagger or three-hook structure — that's acceptable, but I'd flag as medium non-blocking: add per-hook shares to the S1 report, explicitly state that the "rebalance phase-to-hook" lever is GDD-locked, and recommend running the S1 stub before phase stories since the 0.6ms projection will likely trigger a TD budget re-request.

There's also a low-severity ambiguity around M13: the Interaction hook budget description implies a mark_dirty cost, but M13 is APPLY-only, so that cost actually belongs to P2 apply, not the Interaction hook — this needs clarifying.

On the drain caller table, I'm questioning whether Controller, Horror, Interaction, Assembly, and Web Map hooks are truly guaranteed to run after the failure hook — ADR-0019 only pins controller.step before body.integrate after layout.doors, saying nothing about the broader hook graph, so if Controller isn't ordered after power in the compiled sequence, a same-tick drain could occur; I'd amend the table row to reference "per the compiled order" plus a golden test rather than stating it as a fixed rule.

I'm also weighing whether Controller or Assembly even call M14/15/17 — unlikely, so that's low priority too. The ADR's size (150KB, twelve phase files) feels heavy for a solo MVP, though the propagation logic is genuinely the core of the simulation; I'd suggest moving story-level details like scratch inventory and fixture specifics into story acceptance criteria instead, as a low non-blocking note.

Finally, I think RE-1's criterion is too weak — requiring hash equality only "from the first failure hook after t onward" could mask a self-healing divergence, since with full persisted state and deterministic restore, the hash should match at every tick from t+1 onward. I'm checking whether stock reconciliation could cause any legitimate difference, and concluding it shouldn't in this test case, so I'd tighten RE-1 accordingly — this is a medium-severity issue.

Now I'm cross-checking ADR-0011 against ADR-0012: section 7.4(3) rebuilds served_pm in post_restore, section 2.3's last_step_no wording conflicts with the "power hook" framing, and GraphScratch's next/swap behavior — these all look like requests ADR-0012 is making of ADR-0011 that haven't been formally incorporated, meaning ADR-0012 can't be Accepted until ADR-0011 is amended. I want to consolidate these into one cross-ADR item covering the column definitions, last_step_no wording, the HOOK_CURSOR code, and GraphScratch inventory — and I note ADR-0017 actually agrees with ADR-0012's framing, which is reassuring. I'm now looking at whether ADR-0013's check_instantiate naming matches what's assumed elsewhere.

6n+5 also maps to n, confirming the formula up through o≤4; the boot rule capping each step at graph_step_ticks-2 checks out too. For Phase 9, I'm checking whether ensure_derived called inside a hook violates the "never resize in hook path" rule, since it runs after the hook.

I'm also confirming that connectivity changes in phase 9 don't trigger resize, since size_derived is only invoked by structural mutators and phase-driven updates don't alter row counts — though ensure_derived's O(N+E) BFS cost still gets counted against the hook's tick budget in scripted-failure scenarios. I'm cross-checking that TOPO being derived from phase 9 doesn't conflict with the rule that SECTION is never derived from a phase, and noting that the phase 0 stock reconcile hook writing disc_* fields is fine.

I'm now walking through several more edge cases: the hook skeleton that completes early when a scope isn't open, M16's immediate withdraw_store timing, dormant queue entries being dropped at drain, M19's unload behavior when a pending draw exists, and M19's refusal rule around SEAM_ACTIVE versus the WM-24 cut scenario leaving an orphaned dormant section. After working through these, I'm landing on a verdict of CONCERNS, with M19 flagged as a blocking issue.

Separately, I'm considering M14's INIT scope and a P/p_o2 window misclassification, plus whether missing cursor verifier ownership matters — without it, a corrupt cursor could surface as a HOOK_CURSOR fault at runtime, which ties back to ADR-0011's post_restore failure handling. I'm leaning toward marking this non-blocking but cross-ADR, medium severity. Before going further, I should pause and call the advisor as instructed, since I've finished my initial orientation pass.

findings.text: Two mutator scope rows in § 6 contradict their real callers. M19 set_section_dormant is listed as APPLY only, and the Cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0026 says "Web Map calls M19 in a P2 apply". But web-map-and-transit.md WM-7 step (6) calls M19 inside init_world under the shared INIT scope to make A, B and the pod dormant, and ADR-0011's own assumption list puts M19 in INIT. M14 set_load_request is listed as APPLY, HOOK. But ADR-0017 (D3.4 E1, line 565, and its ask at line 978) calls M14 from the INIT-scope E1 and assumes "the INIT-scope deposit drains at the first power hook". The § 5 drain rule has no definition for an INIT deposit. As written, the new-game build would get REFUSED from M19, which fails the build with SL_NEW_GAME_NO_BASELINE, and armed lamps would have no defined drain tick.
findings.amendment: In the § 6 table, set M19's scope phases to APPLY, INIT and M14's to APPLY, HOOK, INIT. Add a row to the § 5 drain table: an INIT deposit drains at phase 0 of the first graph.propagate.power execution after LOADING to RUNNING, which is the first RUNNING tick T with T mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS == hook_offset_power, and that tick matches ADR-0017 D5.2's arm_tick. State that M19 in INIT stamps dormant_since with the INIT step_no (0 for a new game), and that its TOPO/SECTION marks are discarded under ADR-0003 § 4's INIT rule (one ALL batch). Change the ADR-0026 cross-ADR assumption to "M19 in init_world under INIT and in P2 applies (departure, pod_settle, berth, reconcile), never from a Graph hook".

findings.text: The § 11 restore-equivalence table (row 'P, p_o2, o2_pm, trend') calls the intensive caches "pure function of n, V and the persisted p_prev: DERIVED, exact". That contradicts § 2's own note: phase 0 debits n_o2 (the draw drain) and changes t (CHILL/BURN traces through add_heat), while phase 7 recomputes the caches. In the uninterrupted run, P/p_o2/o2_pm/trend therefore hold the values from the previous phase 7 between 6n+0 and 6n+2. A restore landing at 6n+0 or 6n+1 recomputes them in post_restore from the post-draw state and gets different values. Sim-side readers in that window exist: emitter.place every tick, the Interaction and Horror hooks, and Sanity's Perception filter wrapping true_value P, P_O2 and T. This table is the contract the post_restore and RE stories will be built from, so the misclassification would put a restore divergence into the design.
findings.amendment: Choose one and state it in § 2 and § 11. (a) Preferred: at the end of phase 0, recompute the intensive caches (P, p_o2, o2_pm, trend) for every compartment that phase 0 touched (draws and CHILL/BURN). Cost is O(touched), OWN, with no new persisted state. The caches are then a pure function of current persisted state at every tick boundary and the 'exact' label is true. Delete the 'can lag the breath by up to two ticks' note. (b) Otherwise, reclassify the row as a re-derived cache with a window of up to hook_offset_atmo ticks, name its sim readers, and add the case to RE-2's expected-divergence list. Either way, add a restore at 6n+1 after a draw and a BURN to the RE-1/RE-2 fixture set.

findings.text: RE-1 is weaker than the design allows. Every hook product is persisted and the restore is byte-identical, so the graph.state hash should equal the uninterrupted run's at every tick from the restore tick t onward. The ADR only requires equality "from the first failure hook after t onward". That leaves up to five ticks unchecked and would hide a divergence that heals itself, which is the hardest kind to find later.
findings.amendment: In § 11 Tests and in Validation Criteria, require RE-1 equality of the graph.state hash at every tick from t+1 (the first tick executed after the restore). Keep the weaker form only as the documented fallback for the case where ADR-0011 declines the hook-product columns.

findings.text: The spike gating is stated honestly: S1 gates every § 13 budget, and the ladder ends with 'the number moves, not the design'. However, Performance Implications already projects about 0.6 ms per hook at the weld set against the 0.5 ms share, and that figure divides the step evenly by three. The phase-to-hook split is fixed by the GDD (TR-lsg-009). The failure hook (damage over every active node and edge, state evaluation, a possible ensure_derived, and the descriptor build) is plausibly the heaviest, so an even-split estimate understates the worst hook. The spike share is defined per hook tick, so S1 must measure the worst single hook.
findings.amendment: In § 13.1, require S1/S0-f to report P99 and max per hook id (power, atmo, failure) separately, plus the failure hook on a tick where phase 9 triggers ensure_derived. The pass/fail figure against GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS is the maximum over the three hooks, not the step total divided by 3. Correct the Performance Implications sentence to say the even split is an assumption that S1 replaces. Keep Open Question 9 (P3 apportionment) with the technical-director, to be decided on S1's per-hook table.

findings.text: The § 5 caller table claims the Interaction, Emitter State, Horror, Controller, Assembly and Web Map hooks are all ordered after the failure hook. Those orderings belong to sibling ADRs. ADR-0019 says controller.step runs after layout.doors and before body.integrate, and says nothing about the Graph hooks. The general drain rule (the first power hook after the deposit in kernel order) is correct whatever the order turns out to be, but the table asserts facts this ADR does not control.
findings.amendment: Replace the named-hook row with 'any hook placed after graph.propagate.power in the compiled order: the next power-hook tick'. Keep only the edges declared by ADR-0012 or confirmed by an owner (suit.vitals after atmo, attention after power, emitter.place after failure). Name Risk 7's golden compiled-order test as the thing that pins the rest.

findings.text: The pending_draw sort key (cid << 24) | (crew << 8) | arrival_index gives the arrival index 8 bits. The queue bound is MAX_CREW x compartment count: 56 at MVP, but about 480 at VS-A's roughly 120 compartments. Past 255 entries the arrival field carries into the crew field. The order stays deterministic, but the stated (compartment, crew) order is violated. pending_trace's (subject_ref << 16) | (kind << 8) | arrival_index has the same 8-bit field.
findings.amendment: Either add to GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING an assertion that each queue bound is at most 256, or widen the arrival field to 16 bits (for example (cid << 32) | (crew << 16) | arrival_index) and show the D.13 bound for the packed key.

findings.text: The RNG id field is 18 bits and is asserted only at boot against MAX_GRAPH_NODES and MAX_GRAPH_EDGES. That is safe only while ids equal slot counts, i.e. under the MVP no-compaction rule. ADR-0011 sets GraphLimits.ID_MAX = 2^24 precisely because of VS-A id churn. Once compaction or churn lets ids exceed 2^18, node and edge draw keys would overlap again, which is the very defect § 8.2 fixes.
findings.amendment: Do one of two things. Size the id field to GraphLimits.ID_MAX: the counter becomes (step_no << 26) | (kind << 24) | id, and step_no < 2^30 keeps it under 2^56. Or state in § 8.2 that the 18-bit field is MVP-only, and add an id < 2^18 check to the CAPACITY reason of M1, can_join and the RAGGED stub path so that a later change cannot exceed it silently.

findings.text: § 6's Budgets bullet and § 13.6 count 'one mark_dirty per applied M13' against the Interaction hook budget (TR-interact-038). But M13 is APPLY only, and the 10 SYSTEM door resubmits per tick are P2 commands (ADR-0013/ADR-0020). The Graph's M13 cost therefore lands in P2 apply, not in the Interaction hook.
findings.amendment: State that check_set_opening_area and check_set_valve may run in the Interaction hook's reads or validates, while applied M13 writes run in P2 apply. S1 reports the Graph's P2 share under the TR-interact-038 load separately from the hook share.

findings.text: § 4 says ensure_derived builds 'the sizes of the scratch and the descriptor store', and phase 9 calls ensure_derived inside the failure hook. § 3 and § 13.2 say scratch and caches are sized only by structural mutators and post_restore, 'never in a phase'. A reader could take this to mean a resize on the hook path, which would violate HOT-01 and CNT-01.
findings.amendment: Reword § 4: ensure_derived recomputes counts and contents into members already sized by size_derived()/size_scratch(), and calls neither. Phase-driven connectivity changes never change row counts, so the phase-9 call cannot resize. Add the absence of resize to the phase-9 path's HOT-01 coverage.

findings.text: The traceability sentence is off. It says 28 rows carry ADR-0012, then '18 decided here, 11 partial, 13 owned elsewhere'. 18 + 11 = 29 because TR-lsg-020 is volunteered and not planned for ADR-0012. All 28 planned rows (requirements-traceability.md) are covered, so traceability itself is complete; only the count statement is wrong.
findings.amendment: Reword: '28 planned rows, all addressed (18 full, 10 partial); TR-lsg-020 is a residual this ADR adds as partial; 13 further rows are owned elsewhere and supplied here.'

findings.text: Right-sizing advisory. At about 150 KB the ADR carries story-level detail (the scratch inventory, the column-diff harness, per-fixture lists and the full Validation list). That suits the Graph, the simulation's core, but it raises sync cost whenever a sibling ADR or the GDD moves.
findings.amendment: No change is required before Accept. When the Graph epic is created, move the fixture-by-fixture Validation lists into story acceptance criteria and leave the ADR citing them by name.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0012 depends on ADR-0011 amendments that are not yet made. (1) Persisted node columns n_served and n_draw (int32, canonical zero off power consumers) and the CABLE e0 = net-load overlay. § 3.4 currently defines e0 only for DUCT and OPENING, and § 7.4 (3) still rebuilds served_pm in post_restore. (2) Line 134 says hdr.last_step_no is 'the last step whose power hook completed', while ADR-0012 § 1 and ADR-0017's assumption both use the failure hook. (3) A new GraphFaults code HOOK_CURSOR (25 is free; 24 is SATURATION). (4) GraphScratch holds accumulators only (§ 6.2 (4) refined), plus the GraphCaches and GraphDiag members and the derived_members.json entries. (5) ADR-0013 assumes a pure check_instantiate(views, template_id), while ADR-0012 names check_instantiate_section with the extra reason ONSET_UNKEYED.
cross_adr.amendment: Amend ADR-0011 as follows. § 3.2 and § 3.4: add n_served and n_draw, define e0 for CABLE as net load, and update the F-MVP size (about 30.5 KB). § 6.1, § 7.4 (3) and Alternative 7: move served_pm out of DERIVED. § 2.3/line 134: last_step_no = the last step whose failure hook completed. § 8.1: add 25 HOOK_CURSOR. § 6.2: GraphScratch is accumulators only, with ADR-0012 § 3's inventory. Key Interfaces: settle one name and signature for the instantiate check (check_instantiate_section(views, section_id, template_id, kind) returning the LS-18 reasons plus ONSET_UNKEYED) that ADR-0013's can_build calls. ADR-0012 cannot be Accepted before these land.

cross_adr.text: No ADR owns the check of the hook cursors against the restored clock. ADR-0012 assumes ADR-0016's verifier does it (last_step_X equals the step of the last tick at or before T on which hook X was due, with the step-0 convention), but ADR-0016's V1-V16 table has no such row and ADR-0011 § 7.2's ordered restore steps do not mention cursors. Without the check, an inconsistent cursor passes the load and surfaces mid-play as a HOOK_CURSOR fault. Also, hook_offset_* are now GraphTuning data, so a rule phrased as 'the tick on which hook X was due' is undefined if the offsets changed between save and load.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 adds a § 7.2 (or § 7.4) step with a GRAPH_RESTORE_* code. It checks last_step_power/atmo/failure and last_step_no against the restored T under ADR-0012 § 1's rule, using the step-0 convention, and requires last_step_no == last_step_failure. It also states the stance on an offset change across a save: either compare against offsets carried in the graph payload header, or route the change through ADR-0006/0007 catalogue_version gating. ADR-0016 V3/V4 cites the step, and ADR-0012 retargets its cross-ADR assumption from ADR-0016 to ADR-0011.

cross_adr.text: Two INIT-scope calls are missing from ADR-0012's mutator table. ADR-0017's E1 deposits M14 under INIT, and WM-7 (Web Map init_world, ADR-0026) calls M19 under INIT, but ADR-0012 § 6 allows M14 only in APPLY/HOOK and M19 only in APPLY. ADR-0012's assumption on ADR-0026 ('M19 in a P2 apply') also contradicts WM-7 and ADR-0011's assumption.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0012 amends § 6 (M14: APPLY, HOOK, INIT; M19: APPLY, INIT). It adds the § 5 INIT drain rule (first power-hook tick after LOADING to RUNNING, consistent with ADR-0017 D5.2 arm_tick) and corrects its ADR-0026 assumption. ADR-0017 and ADR-0026 need no change.

findings.text: Two mutator scope rows in § 6 contradict their real callers. M19 set_section_dormant is listed as APPLY only, and the Cross-ADR assumption on ADR-0026 says "Web Map calls M19 in a P2 apply". But web-map-and-transit.md WM-7 step (6) calls M19 inside init_world under the shared INIT scope to make A, B and the pod dormant, and ADR-0011's own assumption list puts M19 in INIT. M14 set_load_request is listed as APPLY, HOOK. But ADR-0017 (D3.4 E1, line 565, and its ask at line 978) calls M14 from the INIT-scope E1 and assumes "the INIT-scope deposit drains at the first power hook". The § 5 drain rule has no definition for an INIT deposit. As written, the new-game build would get REFUSED from M19, which fails the build with SL_NEW_GAME_NO_BASELINE, and armed lamps would have no defined drain tick.
findings.amendment: In the § 6 table, set M19's scope phases to APPLY, INIT and M14's to APPLY, HOOK, INIT. Add a row to the § 5 drain table: an INIT deposit drains at phase 0 of the first graph.propagate.power execution after LOADING to RUNNING, which is the first RUNNING tick T with T mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS == hook_offset_power, and that tick matches ADR-0017 D5.2's arm_tick. State that M19 in INIT stamps dormant_since with the INIT step_no (0 for a new game), and that its TOPO/SECTION marks are discarded under ADR-0003 § 4's INIT rule (one ALL batch). Change the ADR-0026 cross-ADR assumption to "M19 in init_world under INIT and in P2 applies (departure, pod_settle, berth, reconcile), never from a Graph hook".

findings.text: The § 11 restore-equivalence table (row 'P, p_o2, o2_pm, trend') calls the intensive caches "pure function of n, V and the persisted p_prev: DERIVED, exact". That contradicts § 2's own note: phase 0 debits n_o2 (the draw drain) and changes t (CHILL/BURN traces through add_heat), while phase 7 recomputes the caches. In the uninterrupted run, P/p_o2/o2_pm/trend therefore hold the values from the previous phase 7 between 6n+0 and 6n+2. A restore landing at 6n+0 or 6n+1 recomputes them in post_restore from the post-draw state and gets different values. Sim-side readers in that window exist: emitter.place every tick, the Interaction and Horror hooks, and Sanity's Perception filter wrapping true_value P, P_O2 and T. This table is the contract the post_restore and RE stories will be built from, so the misclassification would put a restore divergence into the design.
findings.amendment: Choose one and state it in § 2 and § 11. (a) Preferred: at the end of phase 0, recompute the intensive caches (P, p_o2, o2_pm, trend) for every compartment that phase 0 touched (draws and CHILL/BURN). Cost is O(touched), OWN, with no new persisted state. The caches are then a pure function of current persisted state at every tick boundary and the 'exact' label is true. Delete the 'can lag the breath by up to two ticks' note. (b) Otherwise, reclassify the row as a re-derived cache with a window of up to hook_offset_atmo ticks, name its sim readers, and add the case to RE-2's expected-divergence list. Either way, add a restore at 6n+1 after a draw and a BURN to the RE-1/RE-2 fixture set.

findings.text: RE-1 is weaker than the design allows. Every hook product is persisted and the restore is byte-identical, so the graph.state hash should equal the uninterrupted run's at every tick from the restore tick t onward. The ADR only requires equality "from the first failure hook after t onward". That leaves up to five ticks unchecked and would hide a divergence that heals itself, which is the hardest kind to find later.
findings.amendment: In § 11 Tests and in Validation Criteria, require RE-1 equality of the graph.state hash at every tick from t+1 (the first tick executed after the restore). Keep the weaker form only as the documented fallback for the case where ADR-0011 declines the hook-product columns.

findings.text: The spike gating is stated honestly: S1 gates every § 13 budget, and the ladder ends with 'the number moves, not the design'. However, Performance Implications already projects about 0.6 ms per hook at the weld set against the 0.5 ms share, and that figure divides the step evenly by three. The phase-to-hook split is fixed by the GDD (TR-lsg-009). The failure hook (damage over every active node and edge, state evaluation, a possible ensure_derived, and the descriptor build) is plausibly the heaviest, so an even-split estimate understates the worst hook. The spike share is defined per hook tick, so S1 must measure the worst single hook.
findings.amendment: In § 13.1, require S1/S0-f to report P99 and max per hook id (power, atmo, failure) separately, plus the failure hook on a tick where phase 9 triggers ensure_derived. The pass/fail figure against GRAPH_HOOK_BUDGET_MS is the maximum over the three hooks, not the step total divided by 3. Correct the Performance Implications sentence to say the even split is an assumption that S1 replaces. Keep Open Question 9 (P3 apportionment) with the technical-director, to be decided on S1's per-hook table.

Or state in § 8.2 that the 18-bit field is MVP-only, and add an id < 2^18 check to the CAPACITY reason of M1, can_join and the RAGGED stub path so that a later change cannot exceed it silently.

findings.text: § 6's Budgets bullet and § 13.6 count 'one mark_dirty per applied M13' against the Interaction hook budget (TR-interact-038). But M13 is APPLY only, and the 10 SYSTEM door resubmits per tick are P2 commands (ADR-0013/ADR-0020). The Graph's M13 cost therefore lands in P2 apply, not in the Interaction hook.
findings.amendment: State that check_set_opening_area and check_set_valve may run in the Interaction hook's reads or validates, while applied M13 writes run in P2 apply. S1 reports the Graph's P2 share under the TR-interact-038 load separately from the hook share.

findings.text: § 4 says ensure_derived builds 'the sizes of the scratch and the descriptor store', and phase 9 calls ensure_derived inside the failure hook. § 3 and § 13.2 say scratch and caches are sized only by structural mutators and post_restore, 'never in a phase'. A reader could take this to mean a resize on the hook path, which would violate HOT-01 and CNT-01.
findings.amendment: Reword § 4: ensure_derived recomputes counts and contents into members already sized by size_derived()/size_scratch(), and calls neither. Phase-driven connectivity changes never change row counts, so the phase-9 call cannot resize. Add the absence of resize to the phase-9 path's HOT-01 coverage.

findings.text: The traceability sentence is off. It says 28 rows carry ADR-0012, then '18 decided here, 11 partial, 13 owned elsewhere'. 18 + 11 = 29 because TR-lsg-020 is volunteered and not planned for ADR-0012. All 28 planned rows (requirements-traceability.md) are covered, so traceability itself is complete; only the count statement is wrong.
findings.amendment: Reword: '28 planned rows, all addressed (18 full, 10 partial); TR-lsg-020 is a residual this ADR adds as partial; 13 further rows are owned elsewhere and supplied here.'

findings.text: Right-sizing advisory. At about 150 KB the ADR carries story-level detail (the scratch inventory, the column-diff harness, per-fixture lists and the full Validation list). That suits the Graph, the simulation's core, but it raises sync cost whenever a sibling ADR or the GDD moves.
findings.amendment: No change is required before Accept. When the Graph epic is created, move the fixture-by-fixture Validation lists into story acceptance criteria and leave the ADR citing them by name.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0012 depends on ADR-0011 amendments that are not yet made. (1) Persisted node columns n_served and n_draw (int32, canonical zero off power consumers) and the CABLE e0 = net-load overlay. § 3.4 currently defines e0 only for DUCT and OPENING, and § 7.4 (3) still rebuilds served_pm in post_restore. (2) Line 134 says hdr.last_step_no is 'the last step whose power hook completed', while ADR-0012 § 1 and ADR-0017's assumption both use the failure hook. (3) A new GraphFaults code HOOK_CURSOR (25 is free; 24 is SATURATION). (4) GraphScratch holds accumulators only (§ 6.2 (4) refined), plus the GraphCaches and GraphDiag members and the derived_members.json entries. (5) ADR-0013 assumes a pure check_instantiate(views, template_id), while ADR-0012 names check_instantiate_section with the extra reason ONSET_UNKEYED.
cross_adr.amendment: Amend ADR-0011 as follows. § 3.2 and § 3.4: add n_served and n_draw, define e0 for CABLE as net load, and update the F-MVP size (about 30.5 KB). § 6.1, § 7.4 (3) and Alternative 7: move served_pm out of DERIVED. § 2.3/line 134: last_step_no = the last step whose failure hook completed. § 8.1: add 25 HOOK_CURSOR. § 6.2: GraphScratch is accumulators only, with ADR-0012 § 3's inventory. Key Interfaces: settle one name and signature for the instantiate check (check_instantiate_section(views, section_id, template_id, kind) returning the LS-18 reasons plus ONSET_UNKEYED) that ADR-0013's can_build calls. ADR-0012 cannot be Accepted before these land.

cross_adr.text: No ADR owns the check of the hook cursors against the restored clock. ADR-0012 assumes ADR-0016's verifier does it (last_step_X equals the step of the last tick at or before T on which hook X was due, with the step-0 convention), but ADR-0016's V1-V16 table has no such row and ADR-0011 § 7.2's ordered restore steps do not mention cursors. Without the check, an inconsistent cursor passes the load and surfaces mid-play as a HOOK_CURSOR fault. Also, hook_offset_* are now GraphTuning data, so a rule phrased as 'the tick on which hook X was due' is undefined if the offsets changed between save and load.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 adds a § 7.2 (or § 7.4) step with a GRAPH_RESTORE_* code. It checks last_step_power/atmo/failure and last_step_no against the restored T under ADR-0012 § 1's rule, using the step-0 convention, and requires last_step_no == last_step_failure. It also states the stance on an offset change across a save: either compare against offsets carried in the graph payload header, or route the change through ADR-0006/0007 catalogue_version gating. ADR-0016 V3/V4 cites the step, and ADR-0012 retargets its cross-ADR assumption from ADR-0016 to ADR-0011.

cross_adr.text: Two INIT-scope calls are missing from ADR-0012's mutator table. ADR-0017's E1 deposits M14 under INIT, and WM-7 (Web Map init_world, ADR-0026) calls M19 under INIT, but ADR-0012 § 6 allows M14 only in APPLY/HOOK and M19 only in APPLY. ADR-0012's assumption on ADR-0026 ('M19 in a P2 apply') also contradicts WM-7 and ADR-0011's assumption.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0012 amends § 6 (M14: APPLY, HOOK, INIT; M19: APPLY, INIT). It adds the § 5 INIT drain rule (first power-hook tick after LOADING to RUNNING, consistent with ADR-0017 D5.2 arm_tick) and corrects its ADR-0026 assumption. ADR-0017 and ADR-0026 need no change.
